observations_to_check.question: Does the image read as a quiet inhabited observation, with luminous dark romantic softness and a legible person-flower relationship? Record what the actual image suggests first.
Are the visible face contours, chin-length dark bob and fine fringe reasonably preserved? Do not claim true identity, actual age or personality.
Can the viewer actually see the human holding a vellum fold, an opened interval and a moth supported on a fresh flower? Do not infer a precise pollination action from a mood portrait.
Are the open bloom and a closed neighbouring bud visible together, or is their distinction lost? Treat an absent authorial cue as loss of authored realization, not a requester semantic violation.
Are flowers, dark floral ornament, black lace/materials, restrained gold and soft low-contrast dark treatment visibly integrated rather than merely present in the prompt?

Do the holding fingers belong to the pictured person, connect plausibly through the arm, contact the screen edge, and coexist with bench support? Is the moth spatially supported by the flower? Account for uncertainty at the native image scale.

After describing the pixels, compare subtle sensual support/no added fetish/no added surreal/creativity 1 to the frozen intent. Keep technical binding and perceived expression distinct, and leave user preference unverified.
